_about: Domain-Driven Design of a product's solution, for a builder agent: the subdomains and bounded contexts, the context map, the use cases, the event-storming elements (events, commands, reactions, read models, external systems) and the tactical model (aggregates, entities, value objects, rules, services). Sits on `software-architecture` and so on `product`: the product, its personas, roles, requirements, scenarios, policies, terms, decisions and open questions are the product's; the team and the component that carry a context are the estate's. A relation is {domain, range, inverse, definition}. Use A|B for a union.
_summary: Domain-Driven Design of a product's solution: subdomains, bounded contexts and their map, use cases, events, commands, reactions, read models, external systems, aggregates, entities, value objects, business rules, domain services; what each satisfies, who owns it, and whether the builder may build it.
name: Domain-driven design

UseCase.definition: Something a persona or a role does with the product to reach a purpose. The unit the builder plans from; it issues commands, satisfies requirements and is proved by scenarios.

Subdomain.definition: A part of the business problem: core, supporting or generic. Implemented by one or more bounded contexts.

BoundedContext.definition: A boundary inside which one model and one language apply. The unit of ownership, architecture and deployment.

ContextRelationship.definition: How two bounded contexts relate on the context map: the DDD pattern, which side is upstream, and the mechanism that carries the integration.

DomainEvent.definition: Something that happened in the domain that the business cares about, past tense, with a payload. The orange sticky.

Command.definition: An intent to change the domain, imperative, with a payload. Raised by an actor, a policy, a timer or an external system, and handled by an aggregate or a domain service. The blue sticky.

Reaction.definition: A reaction: whenever this event, then that command. The lilac sticky of event storming (its 'policy'); named Reaction because the product's Policy is a rule imposed from outside. Includes sagas and process managers.

ReadModel.definition: The information an actor needs before issuing a command, projected from events. The green sticky.

ExternalSystem.definition: A system outside the product that sends commands or events in, or receives events out. The pink sticky.

Aggregate.definition: A cluster of entities and value objects with one root and one consistency boundary. Handles commands and emits events.

Entity.definition: A thing with identity that persists through change, carrying typed fields.

ValueObject.definition: A thing defined only by its values, immutable, carrying typed fields.

BusinessRule.definition: An invariant, precondition, postcondition or constraint the domain enforces, cited by the aggregates, commands and use cases it binds. Distinct from the product's Policy, a rule imposed from outside; a policy may require a business rule.

DomainService.definition: Domain logic that belongs to no single aggregate, stateless, operating on aggregates and values.

performed_by.definition: The persona or role that carries out the use case.

issues.definition: The command this use case or reaction sends into the domain.

satisfies.definition: The requirement of the product this asset meets. The trace from the design back to the specification: a requirement nothing satisfies is open design work. Widened to the design: a use case satisfies a requirement.

serves.definition: The purpose this exists for: a requirement, journey or feature serves a value proposition; a value proposition serves an objective. The traceability spine an agent walks from a requirement up to the strategy. Widened to the design: the purpose that justifies a use case, a context or a subdomain.

exercises.definition: The requirement or step a scenario is a concrete path through. Widened to the design: a scenario is an acceptance case of a use case.

realised_in.definition: The bounded context that carries the model for this subdomain.

owned_by.definition: The role accountable for this. Ownership sits on a role, not a person, so it survives people moving. Widened to the estate: an asset or a capability is owned by a team. Widened to the design: a bounded context is owned by a team.

between.definition: One of the two contexts this relationship connects. Every relationship has exactly two.

upstream.definition: The context whose model the other side conforms to or translates from; absent for a partnership.

part_of.definition: This belongs to that: a feature to its product or parent feature, a step to its journey. Widened to the estate: a component, interface or store belongs to one system. Widened to the design: everything the builder produces for a context is part of it; a term's meaning holds in one context.

names.definition: The model element this term of the ubiquitous language refers to.

raises.definition: The event that results when this command succeeds.

handled_by.definition: The aggregate or domain service that executes this command.

triggered_by.definition: What starts this command. A timer is recorded as trigger_kind with a schedule, not as a node.

reacts_to.definition: The event that fires this reaction.

projected_from.definition: An event whose payload this read model is built from.

consulted_by.definition: The persona or role that reads this model to decide.

informs.definition: The command issued after reading this model.

sends.definition: A command or event that enters the product from this external system.

receives.definition: An event the product publishes to this external system.

integrated_by.definition: The context that owns the integration with this external system.

precedes.definition: This event comes before that one in the big-picture flow.

about.definition: What a decision settles, or what an open question concerns. Widened to the estate: a decision that shaped an asset, an open question on one. Widened to the design: a decision that shaped an element, an open question (a hotspot) raised on one.

root.definition: The entity through which every change to the aggregate goes.

composed_of.definition: A part held inside this aggregate or entity.

references.definition: This aggregate holds the identity of that one, never the object.

constrained_by.definition: A rule this element must respect. The builder enforces it where the element lives.

operates_on.definition: What this domain service works with.

emitted_by.definition: The aggregate that publishes this event. Derived from the command that raises it.

listens_to.definition: A context that reacts to or projects this event. Derived from its reactions and read models.

applies_to.definition: What a policy prescribes behaviour for. The governance edge: from here, enforced_by says who enforces it. Widened to the design: a policy from outside applies to a context, requires a business rule, binds a use case.

deployed_as.definition: The system or component of the estate that carries this context at runtime.

documented_in.definition: The artifact that formally specifies this: a brief, a PRD, a UX spec. Distinct from source_doc, which is provenance: the document that introduced the fact into the graph, possibly a transcript. Widened to the estate: a design, a review, a standard. Widened to the design: a storming session, a model, a design note.

readiness.definition: Whether the builder may implement this yet.

kind.definition: Core is where the product competes; supporting is needed but not differentiating; generic can be bought.

architecture_style.definition: Styles the context follows: hexagonal, layered, cqrs, event_sourcing, modular_monolith, and so on.

stack.definition: Languages, frameworks and infrastructure the builder must use.

deployment_unit.definition: How the context is deployed: a service name, a module in a monolith, a function group.

readiness.definition: Whether the builder may implement this context yet.

mechanism.definition: What carries the integration at runtime.

payload.definition: Fields the event carries, each as name, type and meaning.
Fields the command carries, each as name, type and meaning.

trigger_kind.definition: What kind of thing starts this command.

schedule.definition: For a timer trigger: when it fires, as a cron expression or in words.

handler.definition: How the command reaches its aggregate. Derived as application_service for every command; state a value to override.

readiness.definition: Whether the builder may implement this command yet.

condition.definition: When the reaction fires, beyond the event itself: a guard in words.

fields.definition: Fields the model exposes, each as name, type and meaning.

readiness.definition: Whether the builder may implement this aggregate yet.

persistence.definition: How the aggregate is stored and loaded. Derived as repository for every aggregate; state a value to override.

construction.definition: How the aggregate is created. Derived as factory for every aggregate; state a value to override.

fields.definition: Fields the entity carries, each as name, type and constraints.
Fields the value object carries, each as name, type and constraints.

kind.definition: Invariant always holds; precondition before a command; postcondition after; constraint on a value.

expression.definition: The rule in a form the builder can implement, if one exists.
